intro: You are now inside Amasya Museum, a museum in Amasya province, founded in 1925. Its halls carry Amasya's finds from the Chalcolithic to the Ottomans. And alongside them rests something rare: six mummies surviving from the Ilkhanid period.
history: The museum was founded in 1925 and later moved to its present building. It follows Amasya's finds from the Chalcolithic to the Ottomans. Its best known holding, though, is the group of Ilkhanid-period mummies found in the tomb chamber of the Seljuk-era Burmalı Minare Mosque.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the mummies and the Hittite and Pontic finds, then the Seljuk carved doors and the Coin collection.
facts: Did you know? The mummies are the bodies of Ilkhanid governors and their families — the only known group in Anatolia preserved this way. And the collection follows the city's layers in a single sequence, from the Chalcolithic through the Hittites and Pontus to the Ottomans.
outro: This brings our tour of Amasya Museum to an end. Before you go, please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for your visit, and enjoy the rest of your day.
